title: Subbing for Chris Kelly and taking over his jobs
summary: Chris sent Howard to jobs under his name; Howard copied his repertoire and gradually gained his own name.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Let me see. So you would substitute with Chris for Roy and take his place sometimes?

Well Chris, you know, it'd take more than one job and so forth like that and he'd go someplace and make up something and it still would be Chris' name and not have three or four jobs at that particular night.
Would he go from one to the other or stay on one?
And use his name on the other thing? Yeah.
Most of the fellas used to do that. I never know if Sam would do anything like that, but most of the other fellas. Neither Pop is still a Stan.
Would people think you were Chris?

Well when I started playing trumpet, I started playing trumpet, I used to play all the favorite numbers that the people I know they'd go for and the only difference they could tell when it would come into the hall, the difference. I'd play all the numbers that he played exactly.
If they didn't know you, did they ever come up to you and say, hello Chris? No, no.

They knew who you were. After I started making a name for myself, well most of the time then after I got the band together and Chris would send me in his place on a job, well they'd sign up with me. And that's how I got real started, you know what I mean? He sent me in, I could do the same thing he was doing, I was younger and so they come to find out, they put it in there and they had more trust in me that I would come. But with the stand outside he couldn't tell the difference.
